accepted.s: Rajendra I’s northern expedition of 1022 CE is particularly associated with which achievement?
o: Defeat of Vijayaditya VII at Kalidindi
Crossing the Ganga and defeating the Pala ruler Mahipala I
Conquest of Madurai and Sri Lanka
Defeat of the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III
accepted.x: In 1022 CE, Rajendra I led a northern campaign, crossed the Ganga and defeated the Pala ruler Mahipala I.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive ruler-and-event association to identify the correct option.
accepted.sec: Rajendra I - Ganga expedition, new capital, Chola Gangam tank, titles  [other exams]

accepted.s: The title ‘Gangaikondachola’ was assumed by Rajendra I after his
o: northern expedition up to the Ganga
victory over the Rashtrakutas at Takkolam
accepted.x: Rajendra I assumed the title Gangaikondachola after his successful northern expedition that reached and crossed the Ganga.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar royal titles by linking the title with the achievement that produced it.
accepted.sec: Rajendra I - Ganga expedition, new capital, Chola Gangam tank, titles  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following titles was associated with Rajendra I?
accepted.x: Kadaramkondan was one of Rajendra I’s titles. Madurai-konda was associated with Parantaka I, Sungam Tavirtta Chola with Kulottunga I, and Vengi Purveshwara with Someshvara I.
accepted.tq: Separate rulers by matching each title with its correct bearer.
accepted.sec: Rajendra I - Ganga expedition, new capital, Chola Gangam tank, titles  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rajendra I established Gangaikondacholapuram as his new capital.
2. The new capital had a Shiva temple.
3. Rajendra I’s northern campaign preceded the establishment of this capital.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Rajendra I founded Gangaikondacholapuram after his northern campaign and associated it with a Shiva temple.
accepted.tq: Check whether the statements form a connected sequence of event, foundation and construction.
accepted.sec: Rajendra I - Ganga expedition, new capital, Chola Gangam tank, titles  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Gangaikondachola was a title of Rajendra I. Kulottunga I was associated with the title Sungam Tavirtta Chola.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped ruler–title pair.
accepted.sec: Rajendra I - Ganga expedition, new capital, Chola Gangam tank, titles  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following was the earliest capital associated with the Sangam Cholas?
accepted.x: Uraiyur was the early Sangam Chola capital. Thanjavur became important under the Imperial Cholas, while Gangaikondacholapuram was established by Rajendra I.
accepted.tq: Use the chronological distinction between early and Imperial Chola capitals.
accepted.sec: Capitals and core region (Uraiyur, Tanjore, Gangaikondacholapuram, Coromandel)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Poompuhar, also known as Kaveripattinam, was associated with which of the following?
o: A later Chola imperial capital in the Kaveri delta
The capital founded by Rajendra I after his Ganga expedition
An early Chola capital and port at the mouth of the Kaveri
The capital founded by Kulottunga I in Visakhapatnam
accepted.x: Poompuhar or Kaveripattinam was an early Chola capital and an important port situated at the mouth of the Kaveri.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an early capital-port from the later imperial capitals.
accepted.sec: Capitals and core region (Uraiyur, Tanjore, Gangaikondacholapuram, Coromandel)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur is associated with which ruler and approximate date?
accepted.x: Rajaraja I is associated with the construction of the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur around 1010 CE.
accepted.tq: Match the monument, ruler and approximate date rather than relying on the capital alone.
accepted.sec: Capitals and core region (Uraiyur, Tanjore, Gangaikondacholapuram, Coromandel)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The core region of the Chola state was primarily the
accepted.x: The Kaveri delta formed the core region of the Chola state and supported its agrarian and political strength.
accepted.tq: Identify the geographical core by distinguishing the principal river delta.
accepted.sec: Capitals and core region (Uraiyur, Tanjore, Gangaikondacholapuram, Coromandel)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The term ‘Coromandel’ is derived from
accepted.x: Coromandel is derived from Cholamandalam, the traditional name connected with the Chola region.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar regional names and their linguistic origin.
accepted.sec: Capitals and core region (Uraiyur, Tanjore, Gangaikondacholapuram, Coromandel)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is included among the UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples?
1. Brihadeeswara Temple, Thanjavur
2. Shiva temple at Gangaikondacholapuram
3. Temple at Darasuram
4. Temple at Poompuhar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples comprise the temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram. Poompuhar is not included in this group.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the location that does not belong to the recognised three-temple group.
accepted.sec: Capitals and core region (Uraiyur, Tanjore, Gangaikondacholapuram, Coromandel)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Battle)
 a. Takkolam
 b. Koppam
 c. Kudalasangamam
 d. Kalidindi

List-II (Principal victor or result)
 i. Cholas under Virarajendra
 ii. Rashtrakutas under Krishna III
 iii. Cholas under Rajendra I
 iv. Rajendra II claimed victory after Rajadhiraja I was killed

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Takkolam was won by the Rashtrakutas under Krishna III; at Koppam Rajendra II claimed victory after Rajadhiraja I’s death; Virarajendra won at Kudalasangamam; Rajendra I’s army won at Kalidindi.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure battle–victor pair and complete the remaining combinations by elimination.
accepted.sec: Battles → participants + victor (Takkolam, Koppam, Kudalasangamam)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Battle of Takkolam, fought in 949 CE, resulted in the defeat of the forces of
o: Parantaka I by Rashtrakuta Krishna III
accepted.x: At Takkolam in 949 CE, the forces of Chola ruler Parantaka I were defeated by the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna III.
accepted.tq: Link the date with the principal opposing rulers and the result.
accepted.sec: Battles → participants + victor (Takkolam, Koppam, Kudalasangamam)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Koppam:
1. It was fought in 1053 CE.
2. Rajadhiraja I was killed in the battle.
3. Rajendra II claimed victory after the death of Rajadhiraja I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Battle of Koppam took place in 1053 CE. Rajadhiraja I was killed there, after which Rajendra II claimed victory.
accepted.tq: Test the date, casualty and succession of command as a single battle sequence.
accepted.sec: Battles → participants + victor (Takkolam, Koppam, Kudalasangamam)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following battles was fought between Virarajendra and Someshvara I?
accepted.x: The Battle of Kudalasangamam, fought around 1062 CE, was between Virarajendra and the Western Chalukya ruler Someshvara I; the Cholas were victorious.
accepted.tq: Use participant-based identification when several battles involved the same rival dynasty.
accepted.sec: Battles → participants + victor (Takkolam, Koppam, Kudalasangamam)  [other exams]

accepted.s: At Kalidindi, Rajendra I’s army defeated
o: Someshvara I and the Western Chalukyas
Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani Chalukyas
accepted.x: At Kalidindi, Rajendra I’s army defeated Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani Chalukyas. The battle was followed by the construction of three Shiva temples by Rajaraja Narendra for fallen Chola commanders.
accepted.tq: Avoid the wrong-ruler trap by separating the Kalyani Chalukya opponents from their battles with later Chola rulers.
accepted.sec: Battles → participants + victor (Takkolam, Koppam, Kudalasangamam)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the Chola–Kalyani Chalukya rivalry?
1. It was essentially a struggle for control of Vengi.
2. After Koppam, Someshvara I assumed the title Vengi Purveshwara.
3. The rivalry was unrelated to the Vengi region.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The rivalry was essentially connected with Vengi, and Someshvara I assumed the title Vengi Purveshwara after Koppam; statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute reversal in the third statement and retain the two connected historical facts.
accepted.sec: Battles → participants + victor (Takkolam, Koppam, Kudalasangamam)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which event enabled Rajendra Chalukya to ascend the Chola throne as Kulottunga I in 1070?
o: The death of Parantaka I and the defeat of the Pallavas
The deaths of Virarajendra and Adhirajendra
The death of Vijayaditya VII and the end of the Rashtrakutas
The victory of Rajendra I at Kalidindi
accepted.x: After Virarajendra and Adhirajendra died around 1070–71, Rajendra Chalukya took the Chola throne as Kulottunga I.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate succession crisis rather than the later consolidation of Vengi.
accepted.sec: Kulottunga I - parentage, titles, embassy to China, succession  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the death of Vijayaditya VII in 1075, Kulottunga I
o: merged Vengi with his Chola dominions
abandoned the Chola kingdom and returned to China
transferred the Chola capital to Uraiyur
accepted.x: After Vijayaditya VII’s death in 1075, Kulottunga I merged Vengi with his Chola dominions and ruled both regions, giving rise to the Chalukya-Chola association.
accepted.tq: Follow the succession event to determine its political consequence.
accepted.sec: Kulottunga I - parentage, titles, embassy to China, succession  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many merchants did Kulottunga I send in his embassy to China?
accepted.x: Kulottunga I sent 72 merchants to China as part of the diplomatic and commercial contact recorded for his reign.
accepted.tq: Treat the merchant count as a direct numerical recall point and compare the close alternatives.
accepted.sec: Kulottunga I - parentage, titles, embassy to China, succession  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The title ‘Sungam Tavirtta Chola’ refers to Kulottunga I’s association with
o: defeat of the Rashtrakutas at Takkolam
establishment of the first Chola capital
accepted.x: Sungam Tavirtta Chola means the Chola who abolished tolls and was associated with Kulottunga I.
accepted.tq: Decode the title through its administrative meaning rather than confusing it with a military title.
accepted.sec: Kulottunga I - parentage, titles, embassy to China, succession  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kulottunga I — Kulottunga Cholapuram at Visakhapatnam
accepted.x: Vengi Purveshwara was a title assumed by Someshvara I after Koppam. Kulottunga I was associated with the Kalinga conquest, Kulottunga Cholapuram at Visakhapatnam and the title Sungam Tavirtta Chola.
accepted.tq: Find the title belonging to the rival Western Chalukya ruler rather than Kulottunga I.
accepted.sec: Kulottunga I - parentage, titles, embassy to China, succession  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following rulers in chronological order of succession to the Imperial Chola throne:
A. Rajaraja I
B. Vijayalaya
C. Rajendra I
D. Aditya I

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The correct succession is Vijayalaya, Aditya I, Rajaraja I and Rajendra I.
accepted.tq: Fix the founder as the first item and then place the successor rulers in sequence.
accepted.sec: Chola succession - founder, successors, chronology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who among the following succeeded Vijayalaya in the Imperial Chola succession?
accepted.x: Aditya I succeeded Vijayalaya and is associated with the overthrow of the Pallavas.
accepted.tq: Avoid the common founder–successor swap by identifying the immediate successor.
accepted.sec: Chola succession - founder, successors, chronology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which ruler assumed the title ‘Madurai-konda’?
accepted.x: Parantaka I assumed the title Madurai-konda after taking Madurai.
accepted.tq: Match the conquest of Madurai with the title derived from it.
accepted.sec: Chola succession - founder, successors, chronology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rajaraja I was also known as Arumolivarman.
2. Rajaraja I ruled from 985 to 1014 CE.
3. Rajaraja I made the Chola state the largest in South India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe Rajaraja I, also known as Arumolivarman, whose reign is dated 985–1014 CE and marked major expansion of the Chola state.
accepted.tq: Verify the ruler’s alternate name, reign period and principal achievement together.
accepted.sec: Chola succession - founder, successors, chronology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Rajendra I’s position in the Chola succession?
o: He became king only after Kulottunga I in 1070.
He was co-regent from 985 and king from 1012 to 1030.
He ruled from 1044 to 1070 after Rajadhiraja I.
He was co-regent from 1012 and king from 1014 to 1044.
accepted.x: Rajendra I served as co-regent from 1012 and ruled as king from 1014 to 1044.
accepted.tq: Separate the co-regency date from the formal reign dates.
accepted.sec: Chola succession - founder, successors, chronology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which event marked the end of the succession line immediately before the accession of Kulottunga I?
o: The death of Parantaka I at Takkolam
The deaths of Virarajendra and Abhirajendra in 1070–71
The defeat of Rajendra I by Mahipala I
The accession of Aditya I after Vijayalaya
accepted.x: The line ended in 1070–71 with Virarajendra followed by Abhirajendra, after which Kulottunga I began the Chalukya-Chola line.
accepted.tq: Use the terminal pair in the succession table to identify the transition to a new line.
accepted.sec: Chola succession - founder, successors, chronology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Chola inscriptions is correct?
1. They record the achievements of Chola kings.
2. They are the most voluminous inscriptions among the South Indian dynasties mentioned.
3. They provide less information about the Cholas than about earlier dynasties.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The extensive recording of royal achievements is why more is known about the Cholas; statement 3 reverses this relationship.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed comparison in the third statement and retain the two evidence-based statements.
accepted.sec: Chola succession - founder, successors, chronology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
